description: TIC Domicílios is the annual household survey on access to and use of information and communication technologies in Brazil, run by Cetic.br, the research centre of NIC.br and a UNESCO Category 2 centre since 2012. Conducted every year since 2005, it maps ICT access in urban households and, since 2008, rural households, and how individuals aged 10 and over use them, with fixed annual modules and rotating modules. Topics include ICT access at home, computer use, mobile phone use, internet use, digital skills, e-government, e-commerce and cultural activities online. The sample is stratified and clustered in several stages, drawn from the latest IBGE census and PNAD household survey, with face-to-face interviews, and indicators follow the ITU-led Partnership on Measuring ICT for Development and the ITU manual for household ICT statistics, so results compare with other countries. An expert group including the Ministry of Communications, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, IBGE and Ipea supports it. Coverage: Brazil, by region, urban and rural area, income and other breakdowns. Format and access: indicator tables, a data visualisation tool, methodology reports and publications on the Cetic.br site, free; the site carries a Creative Commons notice. Caveats: survey estimates with sampling error; household connectivity is self-reported. Simulation uses: household and social exposure to telecom outages, digital divide and vulnerability layers for service disruption studies. Related records: the Anatel open data give network-side statistics, and the ITU indicators give international comparisons.
